description: Stir-fried chicken in a spicy Indo-Chinese chilli-garlic sauce.

name: Veg Manchurian
description: Deep-fried vegetable balls tossed in a tangy Indo-Chinese sauce, a widely popular Nepali restaurant dish.

name: Buff Fry
description: Pan-fried spiced buffalo meat pieces, a common bar/restaurant snack.

name: Newari Khaja Set
description: A restaurant-style adaptation of Samay Baji served as a mixed snack platter with beaten rice, choila, egg, and achar.
main_ingredients: Beaten rice, choila, egg, achar, bara

name: Buff Chowmein
description: Chowmein noodles stir-fried with buffalo meat.

name: Momo Sadeko
description: Boiled/steamed momo tossed cold in a tangy, spicy sesame-mustard oil dressing.

name: Aalu Ko Achar (Karnali style)
description: A Karnali regional variant of potato achar, often incorporating local herbs and less oil due to regional availability.
notes: Regional variation; limited documentation

name: Marcha (Fermentation Starter)
description: A traditional fermentation starter cake made from rice and herbs, used to brew local alcohol like raksi and jaad.

name: Kodo Ko Raksi
description: A distilled alcoholic spirit made specifically from finger millet, common in Gurung/Tamang hill communities.

name: Bhuja (Sukuti mixed)
description: A snack mix combining roasted beaten rice with shredded dried meat and spices, popular as a bar snack.

name: Gundruk Ko Achar
description: A dry, spiced pickle preparation of gundruk mixed with mustard oil rather than cooked into a soup.

name: Simi Ko Tarkari
description: A curry made from broad or green beans, a common household vegetable dish.
image_source: File:Beans Curry.jpg | Wikimedia Commons — Category:Cuisine of Nepal
notes: Filename confirmed via Commons search; not live URL-verified (see resolver script).

name: Tama Ko Achar
description: A tangy pickle made from fermented bamboo shoots.
main_ingredients: Fermented bamboo shoot, mustard oil, spices
image_source: File:Bamboo Shoots Pickle.jpg | Wikimedia Commons — Category:Cuisine of Nepal
notes: Filename confirmed via Commons search; not live URL-verified (see resolver script).

name: Selroti Achar Combo
description: Sel roti served together with spicy potato achar, a common festive breakfast/snack pairing.

name: Karauli Ko Tarkari
description: A curry made from bitter gourd, valued for its distinct bitterness and health benefits.

name: Bodi Ko Tarkari
description: A simple curry made from black-eyed peas, common household dish.

name: Farsi Ko Tarkari
description: A mildly sweet-savory curry made from pumpkin.

name: Iskus Ko Tarkari
description: A light curry made from chayote squash, common in hill households.

name: Tarul Ko Tarkari
description: A curry made from wild or cultivated yam, common in hill and mountain diets.

name: Alu Ko Achar (Dahi)
description: A creamy variation of potato achar mixed with yogurt instead of only mustard oil.
notes: Closely related to Chukauni

name: Masu Ko Momo (Sherpa style)
description: A Himalayan-style momo variant with thicker dough and yak meat filling.

name: Kwati Roti
description: A regional pairing of Kwati soup with flatbread rather than rice.

name: Dahi (Curd)
description: Plain set yogurt, eaten on its own, with rice, or used in cooking; a household staple across Nepal.
image_source: File:Nepali curd.JPG | Wikimedia Commons — Category:Dahi / Bhaktapur
notes: Filename confirmed via Commons search; not live URL-verified.

name: Burger

main_ingredients: Bun, patty (meat or veg), cheese, vegetables, sauce
image_source: File:Cheeseburger.jpg | Wikimedia Commons
notes: Adopted item; not a native Nepali dish, included for market-relevance Filename confirmed via Commons search; not live URL-verified (see resolver script).

name: Chicken Burger
description: A burger with a fried or grilled chicken patty, widely sold at Nepali fast-food outlets.
notes: Adopted item

name: Buff Burger
description: A locally adapted burger using a spiced buffalo-meat patty instead of beef, reflecting local ingredient substitution.
main_ingredients: Bun, buffalo mince patty, spices, sauce
notes: Local substitution since beef is not commonly consumed in Nepal

name: Veg Burger
description: A burger with a fried vegetable or paneer patty, common vegetarian fast-food option.
notes: Adopted item

name: Pizza
description: A baked flatbread topped with sauce, cheese, and toppings; widely available in Nepali cities via both international chains and local pizzerias.
main_ingredients: Flour dough, tomato sauce, cheese, toppings

notes: Adopted item; both chain and local versions exist Filename confirmed via Commons search; not live URL-verified (see resolver script).

name: Chicken Pizza
description: Pizza topped with chicken pieces, one of the most ordered non-veg pizza variants in Nepal.
main_ingredients: Flour dough, tomato sauce, cheese, chicken
notes: Adopted item

name: Veg Pizza
description: Pizza topped with mixed vegetables, a common vegetarian option at Nepali pizzerias.
main_ingredients: Flour dough, tomato sauce, cheese, vegetables
notes: Adopted item

name: Club Sandwich
description: A multi-layer sandwich with bread, chicken/egg, vegetables, and sauce, common on Nepali cafe and hotel menus.
notes: Adopted item; common in cafes and hotels

name: Veg Sandwich
description: A simple sandwich with bread and vegetable filling, a common breakfast/tiffin item in Nepali cities.
notes: Adopted item

name: Chicken Sandwich
description: A sandwich filled with cooked or grilled chicken, vegetables, and sauce.
notes: Adopted item

name: French Fries
description: Deep-fried potato strips, now a near-universal side/snack item in Nepali restaurants and street stalls.

notes: Adopted item Filename confirmed via Commons search; not live URL-verified (see resolver script).

name: Fried Chicken (KFC-style)
description: Batter-coated deep-fried chicken pieces, popular via both international chains and local fast-food outlets.
notes: Adopted item

name: Hot Dog
description: A sausage served in a sliced bun with sauces, sold at Nepali cafes, food courts, and some street stalls.
notes: Adopted item; sausage is often chicken- or buff-based locally rather than beef/pork

name: Pasta
description: Italian-style pasta served with tomato, cream, or mixed sauces, common on Nepali cafe and restaurant menus.
notes: Adopted item

name: Chicken Biryani
description: Spiced, layered rice dish cooked with chicken and whole spices, a South Asian import now common in Nepali restaurants, especially in the Terai and cities.

notes: Adopted item; strongest presence in Terai and urban restaurants Filename confirmed via Commons search; not live URL-verified (see resolver script).

description: Layered spiced rice dish cooked with goat meat, served at restaurants and for special occasions.
main_ingredients: Rice, goat meat, whole spices, yogurt, fried onion
notes: Adopted item

name: Veg Biryani
description: A vegetarian version of biryani made with mixed vegetables and paneer instead of meat.
main_ingredients: Rice, mixed vegetables, whole spices, yogurt
notes: Adopted item

name: Instant Noodles (cooked)
alternate_names: Wai Wai Noodles, Chow Chow, Rara Noodles
description: Packaged instant noodles cooked as a quick soup or dry-fried dish, extremely common as a fast home meal and trekking food across Nepal.
main_ingredients: Instant noodle block, seasoning, egg/vegetables optional
image_source: File:Cooked Rara Noodles.jpg | Wikimedia Commons — Category:Food of Nepal
notes: Wai Wai and Rara are the two dominant Nepali brands; recipe/spice level varies by brand Filename confirmed via Commons search; not live URL-verified (see resolver script).

name: Khasi Sekuwa
description: Skewered, marinated, and grilled goat meat, a premium version of sekuwa served at restaurants and gatherings.

name: Pork Sekuwa
description: Skewered, marinated, and grilled pork, common among Tamang, Rai/Limbu, and other communities that eat pork.

name: Fish Sekuwa
description: Marinated and grilled whole or filleted fish, popular near rivers and lakeside towns like Pokhara.

name: Sukuti Sadeko
description: Rehydrated, shredded dried meat tossed with onion, tomato, chilli, and mustard oil into a tangy, spicy salad, a very popular bar/snack food.
main_ingredients: Dried buffalo meat, onion, tomato, mustard oil, spices
notes: Distinct from plain Sukuti and from the cooked Sukuti curry

name: Batuk
description: Deep-fried black lentil patties similar to Bara, associated with Magar and Khas communities and eaten especially during Maghe Sankranti.

name: Sargemba
description: A traditional Limbu blood sausage made by stuffing pig blood and spices into intestine casing.
notes: Distinct dish from Kinema; regional Limbu specialty with limited documentation

name: Wachipa (Rai Ash Dish)
description: A Kirati Rai dish of minced chicken cooked with rice and ash from burnt chicken feathers, giving it a distinctive bitter, smoky note.
main_ingredients: Chicken, rice, burnt chicken-feather ash, spices
notes: Name collides with a separate fermented-millet drink also called Wachipa in some sources; renamed here to avoid confusion between the two distinct items

name: Phulaura
description: Deep-fried fritters made from buckwheat or lentil flour, a common Far-Western Nepal snack eaten with chutney.

name: Babar Roti
description: A thick, deep-fried rice-flour bread, crisp outside and soft inside, traditional to the Tharu community.

name: Gwaramari
description: A round, deep-fried Newari doughnut-like bread, commonly eaten for breakfast with milk tea.

name: Tarul (Boiled/Fried)
description: Boiled or deep-fried yam eaten plain, traditionally consumed nationwide during Maghe Sankranti alongside sweet potato and ghee.
notes: Simple festival preparation, distinct from the curried Tarul Ko Tarkari already in this dataset

name: Soy Sauce
description: A salty fermented soybean sauce, now a standard condiment for momo, chowmein, and other Chinese-influenced dishes in Nepal.
notes: Adopted condiment; commercially bottled, not home-fermented in most cases

name: Tomato Ketchup
description: Sweet-tangy tomato sauce, widely used with momo, fries, sandwiches, and fast food across Nepal.
notes: Adopted condiment; commercial product

name: Chilli Sauce (Nepali-style)
description: A hot, tangy red chilli sauce used as a dip or cooking sauce for momo, chowmein, and fried snacks.
notes: Often commercially bottled or made fresh at momo/street stalls

name: Mayonnaise
description: A creamy egg or eggless sauce used as a dip or spread, increasingly common with fries, burgers, and sandwiches in urban Nepal.
main_ingredients: Oil, egg or eggless base, vinegar/lemon
notes: Adopted condiment; commercial product

name: Momo Achar
description: The signature tangy, spicy tomato and sesame-based chutney served alongside momo in Nepal.
main_ingredients: Tomato, sesame seeds, timur, chilli, garlic

name: Milk

name: Ghee

notes: Filename confirmed via Commons search; not live URL-verified.
